metadata.title: Know What Kind of Number You Are Looking At
metadata.description: Build the hierarchy of common number sets and classify rational and irrational numbers.

content.text: Keep the sets straight: natural numbers here begin at 1, whole numbers add 0, and integers add the negative counterparts. Rational numbers can be written as p/q with q non-zero; irrational numbers cannot.
Every rational or irrational number is real. A practical decimal test is useful too: terminating or repeating decimals are rational; non-terminating, non-repeating decimals are irrational.
Let's begin with the basic set definitions.
Do not classify by appearance alone. A square root such as √2 can be irrational even though its symbol looks perfectly simple.

Finally, use the midpoint property of rational numbers.
